items.title: Section: Three Clusters of Affliction, Bound to Three Realms

items.zh: 復次，諸煩惱略有三聚。一、欲界繫，二、色界繫，三、無色界繫。問：如是三聚，幾不善？幾無記？答：初聚一分是不善，餘二聚是無記。諸不善者是有異熟，非餘。
items.en: Moreover, in brief, afflictions form three clusters. First, those bound to the desire realm. Second, those bound to the form realm. Third, those bound to the formless realm. Question: of these three clusters, how many are unwholesome, and how many are morally neutral? Answer: a portion of the first cluster is unwholesome; the remaining two clusters are morally neutral. Only the unwholesome ones have a ripening result; the rest do not.

items.zh: 問：幾多性？幾少性？答：初多性，餘不爾。如多性、少性，如是猛利長時染惱性、非猛利長時染惱性，發起外門雜染性、發起內門雜染性，發起惡行性、發起非惡行性，能生多苦性、能生少苦性，大有罪性、小有罪性，遲離欲性、速離欲性，不離欲所顯性、離欲所顯性，三摩地相違性、非三摩地相違性，非一種相生決定性、一種相生決定性等，當知亦爾。

items.title: Section: Eight Questions Every Practitioner Actually Wants Answered

items.zh: 中嗢拕南曰：多、染惱、內門、惡行、生諸苦、有罪、遲離欲、三摩地、生等。復次，云何能斷煩惱？齊何當言已斷煩惱？從何煩惱而可說斷？斷諸煩惱為頓、為漸？云何次第斷諸煩惱？諸煩惱斷，復有幾種？煩惱斷已，有何等相？諸煩惱斷有何勝利？謂善法資糧已積集故，已得證入方便地故，證得見地故，積習修地故，能斷煩惱；得究竟地，當言已斷一切煩惱。
items.en: The verse placed at the chapter's midpoint says: numerous, defiling, external in door; generating evil conduct, generating manifold suffering; culpable, slow to leave desire; opposed to concentration, generating the scattered. Moreover, how is affliction severed? At what point can affliction be said to have been severed? From which affliction can severing be spoken of? Is the severing of affliction sudden or gradual? In what sequence is affliction severed? How many kinds of severing of affliction are there? Once affliction is severed, what marks appear? What benefit does severing affliction bring? Because the provisions of wholesome dharma have already been accumulated, because access to the ground of skilful means has already been attained, because the ground of seeing has been attained, and because habituated practice at the ground of cultivation has continued, affliction can be severed; once the ultimate ground is attained, it can be said that every affliction has been severed.

items.title: Section: Four Kinds of Yoga — Faith, Aspiration, Diligence, and Skilful Means

items.zh: 復有差別。謂由修習四種瑜伽，能斷煩惱；若善修習如是四種，當言已斷一切煩惱。四種瑜伽，如聲聞地已說其相。
items.en: There is a further difference. Through cultivating four kinds of yoga, affliction can be severed; once these four have been well cultivated, it can be said that every affliction has been severed. The four kinds of yoga are as their characteristics were already explained in the Stage of the Hearers.

items.title: Section: Five Steps of Comprehensive Knowing

items.zh: 復有差別。謂相續成熟故，得隨順教故，內正作意故，對治道生故，能斷煩惱。修對治道已到究竟，當言已斷一切煩惱。復有差別。謂了知煩惱事故，了知煩惱自性故，了知煩惱過患故，煩惱生已不堅著故，攝受對治故，能斷煩惱；對治已生，當言已斷一切煩惱。
items.en: There is a further difference. Because affliction's own basis is known, because affliction's own intrinsic nature is known, because affliction's own faults are known, because one does not cling firmly once affliction has arisen, and because the antidote is taken up, affliction can be severed; once the antidote has arisen, it can be said that every affliction has been severed.

items.title: Section: "Skilfully Cultivating Both Together, Only Then Are Both Released"

items.zh: 復有差別。修奢摩他故，修毘鉢舍那故，能斷煩惱；若諸相縛已得解脫，諸麁重縛亦得解脫，當言已斷一切煩惱。如世尊言：相縛縛眾生，亦由麁重縛。善雙修止觀，方乃俱解脫。復有差別。謂了知所緣故，喜樂所緣故，能斷煩惱；所依已滅故，已得轉依故，當言已斷一切煩惱。
items.en: There is a further difference. Through cultivating calming and cultivating insight, affliction can be severed; once the bondage of characteristics has been released, and the bondage of coarse-heaviness has likewise been released, it can be said that every affliction has been severed. As the Blessed One said: mark-bondage binds sentient beings, and coarse-heaviness bondage binds them too. Only by skilfully cultivating both calming and insight are both released together. There is a further difference. Because the object is thoroughly known, and because the object is delighted in, affliction can be severed; because the basis has already been destroyed, and the transformed basis has already been attained, it can be said that every affliction has been severed.

items.zh: 復次，從彼相應及所緣故，煩惱可斷。所以者何？對治道生，煩惱不起，得無生法，是故說名斷彼相應。相應斷已，不復緣境，故從所緣亦說名斷。

items.title: Section: Sudden Breakthrough, Gradual Labour — And Where Practice Actually Begins

items.zh: 復次，見斷煩惱頓斷，非漸。所以者何？由現觀智諦現觀故，能斷見道所斷煩惱。然此現觀與壞緣諦作意相應，是故三心頓斷一切迷苦諦等見斷煩惱。修斷煩惱漸次而斷，數數修道方能斷故。復次，最初應斷不善事業及諸惡見。謂在家者。次復應斷樂出家障。謂欲尋思、恚尋思、害尋思。次復應斷不定心者三摩地障。謂眷屬尋思、國土尋思、不死尋思。次復應斷得作意障。謂樂遠離品身諸麁重。
items.en: Moreover, affliction severed at the path of seeing is severed suddenly, not gradually. Why is this so? Because it is by the direct realisation that truly beholds the truths that the affliction severed at the path of seeing is severed. This realisation corresponds to an attitude directed at renouncing its object, and so, through three minds, all affliction confused about the truth of suffering and the rest, severed at the path of seeing, is severed all at once. Affliction severed by the path of cultivation is severed gradually, only through repeated cultivation of the path. Moreover, one should first sever unwholesome livelihood and wrong views — this refers to householders. Next, one should sever whatever obstructs the joy of renunciation — namely, discursive thought of desire, discursive thought of ill will, and discursive thought of harm. Next, one should sever whatever obstructs concentration for one whose mind is not yet settled — namely, discursive thought of family, discursive thought of homeland, and discursive thought of not dying. Next, one should sever whatever obstructs the attainment of mental application — namely, the body's own coarse-heaviness belonging to the class that delights in seclusion.

items.title: Section: Nine Ways to Name a Single Severing

items.zh: 次復應斷見斷煩惱。次復應斷修斷煩惱。次復應斷屬苦、屬憂、屬樂、屬憙，及屬諸捨諸定障品障礙煩惱。次復有一補特伽羅，應斷所知障品諸障。由此次第，應斷煩惱。復次，諸煩惱斷，當知多種，略則為二。一、諸纏斷，二、隨眠斷。諸纏斷者，謂貪瞋斷乃至疑斷，薩迦耶見斷乃至邪見斷，見苦所斷斷乃至修道所斷斷，欲界所繫斷乃至無色界所繫斷，散亂斷、曉悟斷，羸劣斷、制伏斷、離繫斷。當知離繫斷，即是隨眠斷。
items.en: Next, one should sever the afflictions severed at the path of seeing. Next, one should sever the afflictions severed at the path of cultivation. Next, one should sever whatever hindering afflictions belonging to the class of meditative hindrances are tied to pain, to distress, to pleasure, to joy, and to every neutral state. Next, for a certain person alone, one should sever whatever hindrances belong to the class of the hindrance to what is known. By this sequence, affliction is to be severed. Moreover, the severing of affliction should be known to be of many kinds; in brief, two. First, the severing of manifestation. Second, the severing of latent tendency. The severing of manifestation is severing greed and hatred through doubt, severing self-view through wrong view, severing what is severed by seeing suffering through what is severed by the path of cultivation, severing what is bound to the desire realm through what is bound to the formless realm, and severing at the scattered stage, at the stage of awakening through admonition, at the weakened stage, at the suppressed stage, and at the stage of freedom from binding tie. It should be known that severing at the stage of freedom from binding tie is precisely the severing of latent tendency.

blocks.text: A practical section: where, how, and by what affliction is severed. Its key line: only by cultivating calm and insight together are both released.

Master Cháng Bǎi: desire-realm afflictions are partly unwholesome; higher-realm afflictions are "concealed-neutral", weak, but still obstructing the path. (Untranslated, 0628b04: ten pairs of contrasting traits: many or few, fierce and long-lasting or not, leading to wrong conduct or not, much suffering or little, slow or quick to be left behind, obstructing concentration or not.)

The first: where can affliction be severed? Master Cháng Bǎi: one needs at least access concentration to begin. (Untranslated, 0628c11: affliction is severed in its association and in its object: when the remedy arises, affliction no longer arises, and so no longer takes its object.)
Faith, aspiration, diligence, and skilful means. Master Cháng Bǎi: diligence means day and night working to clear hindrances to calm and insight.
Master Cháng Bǎi: after an affliction arises, one rightly recognises it as wrong and quickly lets it go.
"Skilfully cultivating both together, only then are both released." Master Cháng Bǎi: insight alone becomes dry wisdom; calm alone lacks the wisdom to cut.
Master Cháng Bǎi: seeing the four truths directly is sudden; at cultivation, severing is gradual through repeated practice. Practice begins from outer conduct and moves to subtle obstacles.
Master Cháng Bǎi: one severing is of manifest affliction, the other of seeds; "freedom from bond" means wholly severing affliction's binding.
"Insight alone is dry; calm alone cannot cut." Most of us lean one way. The treatise asks for both.

quiz.q: The English has "the remaining two clusters are neutral." Why is "neutral" a problem?
options: in §§10–13 it means equanimity; here 無記 is moral quality, concealed-neutral, and one word confuses them
no problem: 無記 is equanimity, higher realms' afflictions all joining it
it should be "unwholesome"
it should be "wholesome"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: desire-realm afflictions are partly unwholesome; form- and formless-realm beings also have afflictions, but neutral, that is, concealed-neutral, weak in force and not leading to evil paths. The English "neutral" was used just above for the feeling faculty, so the two senses blur.

quiz.q: What are the three clusters of affliction, and what does 聚 mean?
options: severed by vision, cultivation, adepts; 聚 means a village
upper, middle, lower; 聚 means one time
bound to the desire, form, and formless realms; each gathers many afflictions
greed, hatred, delusion; 聚 means poison
quiz.why: The treatise groups afflictions by realm. Master Cháng Bǎi: 聚 indicates many, and each cluster includes many afflictions. The lost passage after this, on ten pairs of traits, is what the verse in §15 summarises, so the English verse has nothing behind it.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the verse's 外門 and concentration phrases?
options: 外門 means outsiders and the phrase rebirth by absorption
outside the temple; recitation
the body; sleep
the desire realm takes outer objects; higher realms have one mode, determined in one mark
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 外門 means the desire realm's affliction arising through outer form, sound, smell, taste, and touch; form- and formless-realm beings have one kind of object, one-pointed. The English "opposed to concentration, generating the scattered" is an interpretive paraphrase.

quiz.q: How is affliction severed, and at what point is it said to be severed?
options: by giving and ethics, all being severed on taking bodhisattva precepts, ethics being the root of merit, unrelated to any ultimate ground
by recitation alone; severed at death
by provisions, skilful means, seeing, and cultivation; at the ultimate ground, all are severed
by austerity alone; severed on reaching heaven
quiz.why: The first of eight questions most on practitioners' minds. Master Cháng Bǎi: one needs at least the power of access concentration to begin severing. Grounds of provisions, skilful means, seeing, and cultivation are the means; the ultimate ground is the mark of completion.

options: ethics, absorption, wisdom, liberation, the outline of the Hearers' Stage, unrelated to faith and aspiration
sitting, lying, walking, standing
faith, aspiration, diligence, and skilful means, as in the Hearers' Stage
giving, kind speech, benefit, cooperation
quiz.why: The treatise refers to the Hearers' Stage. Master Cháng Bǎi explains faith yoga as faith and purity of mind; diligence as day and night working to clear hindrances to calm and insight; and means as skill in method. The section title in English names the four, though §16's text does not.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 善修習?
options: sitting eight hours daily, regardless of method
practising in a good monastery
practising under a famous teacher
proper attention, skilful means, repeated practice until very familiar
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: well cultivating means proper attention, skilful means, and repeated practice to full familiarity. Through such practice one becomes able to sever affliction. The English "well cultivated" is fine.

quiz.q: What are the five, such as knowing affliction's basis, and what is said when the antidote arises?
options: knowing greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, doubt; even with the antidote nothing is yet severed until buddhahood
the three realms, vision, cultivation
the five aggregates; severed on absorption
basis, nature, faults, no clinging once arisen, taking up antidote; with it arisen, all are severed
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the place on which affliction depends, its cause, is its basis; after an affliction arises, one rightly recognises it as wrong and quickly lets it go. The English "does not cling firmly" conveys 不堅著.

quiz.q: How do calm and insight release the two bonds?
options: calm frees from marks and insight from heaviness
calm alone suffices
insight alone suffices
severing clinging to marks and seeds; insight alone is dry, calm alone lacks wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one needs to sever the mind's clinging to objects' marks and sever affliction's seeds; insight alone becomes dry or wild wisdom, and calm alone lacks the wisdom to sever. This verse is one of the key statements of the Yogācāra path, and the English keeps it well.

quiz.q: Knowing and delighting in the object sever affliction. What marks completion?
options: the body gone, so that only after death is affliction severed, not even a living arhat qualifying
absorption and powers
full ordination
the basis has been destroyed and the transformed basis attained
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the object of calm and insight must be clearly known; the affliction seeds in the store-consciousness are wholly removed, it turning from the defiled to the pure side; delight gives motive force. So the basis destroyed is the defiled seeds, not the living body.

options: severed by vision, sudden; by cultivation, gradual, through repeated practice
vision gradual; cultivation sudden
both sudden
both gradual
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: directly witnessing the true aspects of the four truths is the realisation that beholds them; at cultivation, severing is gradual through repeated practice. Delusion about truth goes at once, like darkness at sunrise, while deep habit takes long.

quiz.q: The English has "in three mind-moments." What is the problem?
options: no problem: three moments are very brief, hence sudden, the lecture saying they arise in sequence, without any clash
it should be "three lifetimes"
the three minds are three wisdoms, not moments; "mind-moments" also clashes with "all at once"
it should be "three hearts"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 壞緣 means turning away from the formations of suffering and origin; inwardly removing false discrimination of self yields the wisdom of the emptiness of self. The three minds are three wisdoms. "Mind-moments" is an addition, and it clashes with the next words, "all at once."

quiz.q: What is the order from the start to the obstacle to attention, and why does thought block concentration?
options: first bodily heaviness, then family thoughts, then desire thoughts, then evil deeds
first the cognitive hindrance
first cultivation, then vision
evil deeds and views; three thoughts; three further thoughts; bodily heaviness; thoughts gravely obstruct concentration
quiz.why: The sequence runs from outer conduct to subtle obstacles. Master Cháng Bǎi: these three kinds of thought greatly hinder absorption, and one should observe their faults. Next come the afflictions severed by vision and by cultivation, then hindrances to absorption, then the cognitive hindrance.

quiz.q: After vision and cultivation, what remains, and what must "a certain person" sever?
options: hindrances to absorptions; a bodhisattva, cognitive hindrances
upper-grade afflictions of cultivation; an arhat must sever the hindrances, lacking absorption, unrelated to bodhisattvas
nothing remains
ordinary beings, views
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first absorption leaves the sorrow faculty and the second the pain faculty; one on the bodhisattva path must sever not only the affliction hindrance but also what gives rise to the cognitive hindrance. So "a certain person" is the bodhisattva.

quiz.q: What are the two severings, and to which does freedom from bond belong?
options: vision and cultivation; it belongs to vision
worldly and transcendent; it is worldly
of manifestation and of latency; it is severing of latency
sudden and gradual; it is sudden
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one is the severing of manifest affliction, and the other the severing of its seeds; freedom from bond means wholly severing affliction's binding. Earlier severings only weaken or suppress. The English "freed from binding tie" is close.

quiz.q: The English has "as scattered, as awakened..." What is the problem?
options: no problem: the practitioner severs while scattered, wakes, weakens, and is subdued, four stages of change, as the lecture says
it should be "as cold, as hot"
the five sever afflictions at five stages; "as scattered" misleads, and "awakened" is worst, confusable with §5
it should be "as quickly, as slowly"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: subduing affliction and thinning its force is severing by weakening. The Sub-commentary pairs the five with five antidotes, 曉悟 with remorse and admonition. So each names how an affliction is removed. "As awakened" cannot be right, and clashes with §5's term.
